title: Mapping the distribution and historical preservation of lipophilic marine algal toxins in sediments of the Bohai and Northern Yellow seas
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 206 Author(s): Haoshun Zhang, Xiuping He, Tongzhu Han, Xiaofei Yin, Junhui Chen
abstract: The marine benthic environment provides habitat for many fishery organisms. Lipophilic marine algal toxins (LMATs) can accumulate in coastal sediments, where they pose risks to benthic ecosystems and fishery organisms through trophic transfer. However, understanding of the distribution and burial patterns of LMATs in coastal sediments remains limited. Here, LMATs in surface sediments, porewater, and box sediment cores from the Bohai Sea and the northern Yellow Sea of China were systematically investigated. The composition, phase partitioning, spatial distribution, and vertical distribution of LMATs were characterized, and the suitability of sedimentary LMATs as biomarkers was assessed. Thirteen LMATs were detected in the sedimentary environment, including pectenotoxin–2 (PTX2), okadaic acid (OA), azaspiracid–1 (AZA1), azaspiracid–2 (AZA2), gymnodimine (GYM), yessotoxin (YTX), hydroxy–yessotoxin (h–YTX), two PTX2 homologs, and four PTX2 isomers, with the PTX2 isomers reported for the first time in marine sediments. In surface sediments from the Bohai Sea and the northern Yellow Sea, PTX2 (including isomers) was the dominant LMAT, accounting for an average of 56.88%, followed by YTX and h–YTX. PTX2 and OA were the principal LMATs in porewater and exhibited different partitioning behaviors at the sediment–porewater interface. ∑LMAT concentrations in sediments of the northern Yellow Sea (mean 248.5 ng/kg) were significantly higher than those in the Bohai Sea (mean 98.3 ng/kg), with elevated values near the coastal areas of Qinhuangdao (Hebei Province) and Weihai (Shandong Province). ∑LMAT concentrations generally decreased with increasing depth in sediment cores. OA, YTX, and h–YTX were restricted to upper core sections, whereas PTX2 and AZA2 occurred throughout the cores and showed localized concentration maxima at specific depths. Overall, PTX2 and AZA2 exhibit strong stability in deep sediments and show potential as biomarkers for reconstructing the historical occurrence of marine toxigenic algae.

title: Tracing Nutrient Uplift from Permafrost Thaw Using Radiogenic Sr Isotopes in Plants: A Field-Based Soil Warming Experiment
description: Publication date: Available online 28 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Philippe Roux, Damien Lemarchand, Edward Schuur, Sophie Opfergelt
abstract: Permafrost thaw in Arctic ecosystems is altering soil structure and hydrology, deepening the active layer and increasing the availability of nutrients previously locked in frozen ground. These changes contribute to the current trend of increased plant productivity and shifts in species composition. Because arctic plant functional types have specific nutrient acquisition strategies due to differing rooting depths, it is therefore essential to identify the mechanisms responsible for changes in nutrient sources during permafrost degradation. The aim of this study is to quantify the contribution of biological cycling and/or water table rise to nutrient sources available to four major plants upon permafrost thaw. To do so, we developed a mass balance model based on an eight-year soil warming experiment on the Eight Mile Lake study site in Interior Alaska. This model combines vegetation composition survey, water table depth data with foliar strontium (Sr) concentrations and isotopic composition (87Sr/86Sr) to simulate Sr transfer in the soil-plant system. Our results show that biocycling alone is sufficient to explain the isotopic shift under control conditions for all four plants. Under soil warming, however, biocycling accounts for 37-54% of the observed shift for shallow and intermediate rooted species, while water table rise accounts for 35-47%. Although all modelled values remain within the range of observed variability, 2-20% of the observed shift remains unresolved across species. While permafrost thaw is a key source of newly available nutrients, our model suggests that redistribution mechanisms are the primary drivers of changes in plant nutrient sources.

title: Hydrothermal fluids from the Eastern Himalaya Syntaxis and Tengchong Volcanic Field, southeast Tibet: Geochemical constraints on deep-sourced carbon contributions
description: Publication date: Available online 27 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Jujing Li, Zhengfu Guo, Wenbin Zhao, Xiangang Xie, Yutao Sun, Guichun He
abstract: Volcanoes and large-scale strike-slip faults constitute primary conduits for transporting deep-sourced fluids, including carbon, to the Earth’s surface. However, comparative studies that link geothermal anomalies with deep carbon fluxes, as well as the mechanisms governing regional fluid circulation, remain scarce. Here we present a systematic hydrogeochemical investigation of thermal springs from the Eastern Himalayan Syntaxis (EHS) and the Tengchong Volcanic Field (TVF) in southeastern Tibet, integrating major ion compositions, stable isotopes (δD, δ18O), and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) isotopes. Our results show that TVF springs are predominantly of Na–HCO3 and Na–Cl types, whereas EHS springs exhibit Na–HCO3, Na–Cl, and Ca–HCO3 types. Rehai (TVF) springs of the SO4 type suggest a magmatic heat effect. Based on oxygen and hydrogen isotope data, recharge elevations range from 4182 to 5397 m for the EHS and from 1530 to 2637 m for the TVF. Geothermometry reveals distinct circulation depths: 2205–5464 m in the EHS core zone, decreasing to 978–1861 m in the west. Qualitative water-rock interaction analysis supports a dominant role of deep-sourced carbon. By combining our DIC data with previously published gas CO2 compositions from the same springs, we quantitatively estimate that deep-sourced carbon (mantle- and metamorphic-derived CO2) contributes 57.5–93.9% of the spring DIC pool in both regions. Our findings offer new constraints on the contribution of continental collision zones to endogenic CO2 fluxes and their potential implications for long-term climate evolution.

title: Multi-parameter soil gas geochemistry and fracture-controlled degassing along the İzmir Fault (Western Türkiye)
description: Publication date: Available online 27 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Mutlu İçhedef, Caner Taşköprü, İlayda Sapmaz, Fulsen Özen, Gözde Duman, Emre Tabar, Hasan Sözbilir, Salvatore Giammanco
abstract: In this study, soil gas concentrations of 222Rn (Radon), 220Rn (Thoron), and CO2 were measured along the İzmir Fault Zone in western Türkiye to investigate the relationship between gas anomalies and fault-controlled permeability. A total of 342 measurement points were systematically sampled along the two segments of the İzmir Fault (IF), spatial variations of soil gas concentrations were analyzed to identify locations that indicate anomalies. 222Rn (Radon), 220Rn (Thoron), and CO2 concentrations were determined in soil gas in the areas surrounding the fault. Quantile–quantile (Q–Q) plots were used to determine anomaly thresholds for each parameter, and concentration values exceeding these thresholds were classified as anomalies. The results reveal significant spatial variability in soil gas concentrations along the fault system. Although anomalies were detected in both segments of the İzmir Fault, multiple gas anomalies were predominantly concentrated at the westernmost end of the Balçova–Narlıdere segment. This result suggests the following regarding fault activity: The concentration of multi-gas anomalies along the Balçova–Narlıdere segment suggests active degassing processes along this part of the fault. This pattern suggests that gas distribution in the study area is not solely controlled by distance to the main fault line, but may instead reflect the heterogeneous permeability structure of the fault zone and the influence of localized fractures and preferential migration pathways. These findings demonstrate that integrated soil gas measurements provide an effective geochemical approach for identifying structurally controlled gas migration pathways and localized degassing zones in active tectonic environments.

title: Optimizing acid digestion protocols for osmium isotope analysis of Quaternary marine sediments
description: Publication date: 20 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 719 Author(s): G.A. Goss, A.D. Rooney
abstract: The marine osmium (Os) isotope system has become a powerful proxy for reconstructing Quaternary Earth surface processes, owing to its favorable geochemical properties and advances in analytical precision. However, variations in acid digestion protocols, particularly chromic acid (CRA) versus inverse aqua regia (IAR), produce systematic offsets in reported Os isotopic compositions and concentrations from the same sediment samples. These discrepancies arise from the differential dissolution of mineral phases resultant from the variable acids used in such studies. Here, we compare Os isotopic compositions and concentrations from Pleistocene North Atlantic marine sediments digested with CRA and IAR, integrating X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy coupled with electron backscatter diffraction of bulk sediments and post-digestion residues. Digestion via CRA consistently yields more radiogenic Os isotope ratios and lower concentrations than IAR. Analysis of post-digestion residues demonstrates that both methods primarily dissolve carbonates, while silicates and accessory minerals persist at varying degrees. These contrasting dissolution behaviors suggest CRA is more appropriate for sediments with low detrital input, while IAR can amplify detrital contributions. Our results highlight the critical need for standardized digestion protocols to ensure reproducible and comparable Os isotope chemostratigraphic records in both early Earth history and Quaternary sedimentary successions.

title: Geochemical and hydrological controls on aragonite versus calcite precipitation in speleothems and paleoclimatic implications
description: Publication date: 20 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 719 Author(s): Rui Zhang, Haiwei Zhang, Christoph Spötl, Carlos Pérez-Mejías, Zixin Guan, Heather Stoll, Yanjun Cai, Liangcheng Tan, Fudong Wang, Xunlin Yang, Yan Yang, Lijuan Sha, Jian Wang, Yina Song, Pengzhen Duan, Youfeng Ning, Hai Cheng
abstract: Speleothem mineralogy (aragonite vs. calcite) and geochemical signatures are governed by complex hydrological and geochemical processes. However, previous studies have predominantly focused on geochemical constraints, whereas the role of cave hydrological processes in regulating carbonate polymorphism has received far less attention. Furthermore, long-term in situ monitoring of the environmental conditions controlling aragonite and calcite precipitation in natural cave settings remains limited. Here, we combine three years of cave monitoring in Shennong Cave, southeastern China, with glass-plate observations and a global dripwater compilation to show that carbonate polymorphism is governed by threshold effects in Mg/Ca–calcite saturation index (SIcc) space, and that precipitation-driven prior carbonate precipitation (PCarbP) favors aragonite precipitation by increasing Mg/Ca while maintaining relatively low SIcc. At Mg/Ca values ≥ 1000 mmol/mol, Mg/Ca defines the threshold for aragonite occurrence and crystal elongation, whereas pH and SIcc are most closely associated with depositional proportion and crystal habit, respectively, with aragonite evolving from slender needles to shorter, thicker bundles as supersaturation increases. At aragonite-precipitating sites, PCarbP during wetter periods drives spatial partitioning of carbonate polymorphs on glass plates, with calcite precipitating at the drip-impact point and aragonite toward the margins, providing direct modern-process evidence for calcite–aragonite fabrics in speleothems. Monitoring results further show that aragonite- and calcite-precipitating sites differ in their hydrological setting, the extent of PCarbP, and the magnitude of Mg/Ca fluctuations. At the seasonal scale, reduced effective infiltration and intensified in-cave degassing drive substantial Mg/Ca increases at aragonite-precipitating sites, whereas lower soil and epikarst pCO2 primarily enhances PCarbP at calcite-precipitating sites. At the interannual scale, dripwater Mg/Ca declined from approximately 2000 to 500 mmol/mol from 2022 and 2025, broadly tracking the long-term increase in regional precipitation. Overall, this study demonstrates how cave hydrology and PCarbP control carbonate polymorphism in cave systems, and indicates that dripwater Mg/Ca reflects different hydroclimatic controls across seasonal and interannual timescales, improving the interpretation of speleothem mineralogy and geochemical proxies in paleoclimate studies.

title: Mineral phase transformation drives molecular fractionation of dissolved organic matter during organic acid-driven weathering of bauxite residue
description: Publication date: 20 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 719 Author(s): Chenglong Lu, Songlin Wu, Fang You, Dingyi Yu, Jitraporn Vongsvivut, Annaleise Klein, Lars Thomsen, David Parry, Ting-Shan Chan, Longbin Huang
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) sequestration is critical to soil formation of bauxite residue (BR) in which BR undergoes mineral weathering and neutralization / acidification driven by microbial and/or plant root-derived organic acids (OA). The present study aimed to understand the molecular fractionation and adsorption of DOM in BR minerals during key stages of mineral weathering and neutralization, using mixed organic acids to simulate the mineral weathering process in the ecological engineering context. Selective adsorption and molecular fractionation of DOM derived from microbial decomposition of plant mulch were characterized using the high-resolution electrospray ionization Orbitrap mass spectrometry (Orbitrap-MS). The OA-treatments progressively weathered sodalite-like alkaline minerals to form amorphous Al/Si/Fe phases and lowered pH, increasing surface reactive sites in mineral phases. The slightly weathered (pH 9–7) and highly weathered and acidified BR minerals (pH 5–4), preferentially adsorbed high-molecular-weight organics rich in aromatic and/or polyphenolic domains. Synchrotron-based Al, Si, and Fe K-edge X ray absorption spectroscopic analyses (XAS) and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) mapping, revealed strong associations of secondary Al/Si/Fe phases with protein-, carboxylic-, aromatic-, and oxygenated lipid-like compounds. These findings highlight the critical role of mineral weathering in BR for controlling the stabilization of DOM during eco-engineered soil formation processes.

title: Trace element composition of cold-water corals from coastal Antarctic surface sediments: Implications for biomineralization mechanisms and paleoceanographic reconstructions
description: Publication date: 20 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 719 Author(s): Derong Zhao, Sang Chen, Junru Guan, Haihong Wu, Xin Chen, Cong Zeng, Zhekai Tang, Maojun Yan, Ning Zhao, Liqiang Xu, Meng Zhou
abstract: The Southern Ocean is one of the most sensitive regions to ongoing climate change, and plays an important role in the global ocean circulation and carbon cycle through a range of physical, chemical and biological processes. Understanding long-term environmental changes in the Southern Ocean can help us better resolve the key processes influencing its impact on global climate. Paleoceanographic reconstructions in the Southern Ocean, however, are often challenging due to a lack of feasible archives and well-calibrated environmental proxies. Cold-water corals are a type of benthic organism of relatively high abundance in the Southern Ocean, with their calcium carbonate skeletons that can potentially record environmental changes at relatively high temporal resolution. Here we report measurements of the trace element composition of cold-water corals and a tubeworm collected from surface sediments in the Ross Sea and west of the Amundsen Sea. We find that spatial distribution of calcitic and aragonitic corals in the Southern Ocean is likely controlled by the bottom water carbonate saturation state. Trace element composition of the biogenic carbonates is mainly determined by their respective mineralogy and displays significant vital effects. Different element-to‑calcium ratios show strong correlations in individual organisms that are similar to cold-water corals found in other regions, and can generally be explained with existing biomineralization models. Several elemental ratio proxies show relations with environmental conditions that are consistent with global calibrations, most notably the Li/Mg-temperature relation in both biogenic aragonite and high-Mg calcite, yet large uncertainties remain in terms of their use in paleoceanographic reconstructions. Understanding the biomineralization mechanisms underlying the vital effects in different types of cold-water corals with in-situ analytical techniques and numerical models is a key step in improving the proxies that are suitable for the extreme environmental conditions in the Southern Ocean.

title: Geochemistry of Amazonian ironstone microbialites and their significance as paleoenvironmental archives
description: Publication date: 5 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 718 Author(s): Marília Prado Freire, Cécile Gautheron, Stéphane Guédron, Bastien Wild, Sylvain Campillo, Sabine Sentenac, Rachel Martin, Valérie Magnin, André Oliveira Sawakuchi, Cristiano Mazur Chiessi, Dailson A. Bertassoli, Ana Maria Goes
abstract: New type of paleoclimatic and paleoenvironmental archives are critically needed in tropical continental areas to better reconstruct multimillennial to multimillion year climate and environmental changes, as classical archives such as speleothems or well-preserved sediments are frequently not available because they are poorly preserved. We examined Pleistocene continental ironstones that are laminated ferruginous crusts formed by the lithification of ferruginous microbialites made of goethite that entrapped coarse to fine siliciclastic grains at different scales (micrometer to few centimeters). Samples were collected from ironstones, formed and exposed in the rapids of the Xingu River, eastern Amazonia (Brazil). Major, trace, and rare earth elements (REE) composition from the microscale to the mesoscale were analyzed in different ironstone samples together with bacterial and fungal diversity to examine their potential as paleoclimatic and/or paleoenvironmental archives. Results indicate that ferruginous ironstones, are composed of finely laminated goethite that conserve their geochemistry after fossilization and have not been affected by secondary diagenetic processes. Changes in Al and P composition in particles entrapped within the goethite lamina and the whole samples are associated with enrichment in redox sensitive elements (e.g., As, V), which can be attributed to periods of lower river hydrological regime. In contrast, coarser and heterolithic ironstone, i.e., ferruginous sandstone trapping quartz grains, with aluminosilicates and psilomelane (MnBa rich mineral) rich in metals (e.g., Pb, Hg, REE) and refractory elements (e.g., Ti, Rb, Zr) were attributed to wetter epochs and higher river water regime. Secondary psilomelane phases are also observed in fracture showing a late precipitation after the ironstone fossilization. From published dating of a decimetric laminated ironstone layer, it is estimated that each laminae recorded information at the decadal to secular scale. The combination of micrometric to mesoscopic geochemical data supports that high resolution studies of Xingu laminated ironstones will provide major insights into paleoclimatic and paleoenvironmental changes in the Amazon basin by focusing on both lithotypes of the ironstones.

title: Distribution and migration pattern of lithium in two tonsteins inside the Li-rich coal under groundwater and seawater leaching
description: Publication date: 5 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 718 Author(s): Huidi Hao, Bo Jiu, Wenhui Huang, Zhenguang Shang, Zhaoguo Wang, Li Long, Linghao Huang, Yingying Zhao, Haonan Chen
abstract: The migration and enrichment mechanisms of lithium (Li) in coal-hosted tonsteins under groundwater and seawater leaching are poorly understood. This study investigates two tonstein samples from the Late Carboniferous No. 6 coal seam in the Jungar Coalfield, Ordos Basin, China, using an integrated approach that combines mineralogical, bulk-geochemical, and in-situ microanalytical techniques (TIMA, SEM-EDS, LA-ICP-MS) to elucidate the role of fluid-rock interactions in Li redistribution. The Li in the upper tonstein was primarily influenced by groundwater and occurs as lattice-bound Li within vermicular kaolinite, which replaced Al3+ through isomorphic substitution (Al3+ + Li+ → Si4+). Furthermore, the Li content in this unit exhibits a distinct trend of increasing in coarser crystals. In contrast, Li in the lower seawater-leached tonstein was initially scavenged via surface complexation onto the high-surface-area cryptocrystalline kaolinite and subsequently stabilized. Fluid composition exerts a key control: while the primary Li source was the volcanic precursors, seawater infiltration, indicated by high Sr/Ba ratios, elevated boron contents, and Mg/Sr signatures in the fracture-filling calcite, significantly enhanced Li mobilization and its subsequent adsorption onto clay surfaces, whereas groundwater of terrestrial origin showed limited mobilization and transport efficiency. Furthermore, the systematic decrease in Li concentrations away from calcite-filled fractures confirms their role as primary conduits for seawater infiltration, while coal permeability and the organic matrix governed the spatial heterogeneity of enrichment. This study characterizes the mechanisms of Li accumulation in tonsteins by comparing the contrasting roles of seawater and meteoric groundwater. Our findings demonstrate that seawater leaching of volcanic precursors is a significantly more effective driver for Li super-enrichment than meteoric groundwater leaching, thereby providing a more precise framework for assessing the potential of Li resources in coal-bearing sequences.

title: Hydrothermal perturbation controls clumped isotope heterogeneity in deep-buried carbonates
description: Publication date: Available online 30 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Yuhe Guo, Yangrui Guo, Jianfang Hu, Wenfeng Deng, Gangjian Wei
abstract: Carbonate clumped isotope (Δ47) thermometry is widely used for paleotemperature reconstruction, but its modification by hydrothermal activity in tectonically active basins remains poorly constrained. Here we investigate Δ47 heterogeneity in Late Ordovician deep-buried carbonates from the Wanhe section, South China, using stable isotopes, trace elements, and thermal conduction modelling. Results show Δ47-derived temperatures range from 47 to 194 °C, forming a vertical gradient that cannot be explained by background geothermal gradients (<2 °C for ~50 m) or solid-state reordering. Fluid-rock interaction modelling indicates carbonate recrystallization occurred under closed-system, low water-rock ratios (~0.01–0.1). Thermal conduction simulations demonstrate that a single hydrothermal vein at the section base generates an exponential thermal decay, broadly consistent with measured temperatures. Elevated Mn/Ca, reduced Sr/Ca, and bright orange cathodoluminescence further support hydrothermal alteration. Our findings reveal that hydrothermal perturbation controls Δ47 heterogeneity, which may be misinterpreted as primary signals when relying solely on standard macroscopic screening. This study highlights the necessity of excluding hydrothermal overprinting in tectonically active basins and provides a diagenetic framework for assessing geochemical proxy reliability in deep-time carbonates, with three key diagnostic criteria for identifying cryptic hydrothermal overprinting: (1) an anomalous vertical T(Δ47) gradient over short stratigraphic intervals (<100 m) that cannot be explained by background geothermal gradients; (2) elevated Mn/Ca and reduced Sr/Ca ratios in altered samples; and (3) evidence of closed-system, low water/rock ratio recrystallization from δ18O-Δ47 systematic.

title: Carbonate triple oxygen and carbon isotope effects of chemical pretreatments on tooth enamel and eggshell
description: Publication date: Available online 28 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Sarah A. Katz, Alex Bertacchi, Drake A. Yarian, Jordan A.G. Wostbrock
abstract: Carbon (δ13C) and oxygen (δ18O) isotope values of biominerals are widely used to infer information about ancient environments, ecosystems, and climatic conditions. However, organic and/or diagenetic contaminants can impact measured isotope values and compromise interpretations. Commonly, researchers chemically pretreat biominerals to minimize these contaminants and the effects of different chemical pretreatments on mineral structure, δ13C, and δ18O values have been extensively documented. Recently, terrestrial biomineral triple oxygen isotope values (Δ′17O; paired δ17O and δ18O measurements) have emerged as a proxy of global primary production, atmospheric pCO2, animal physiology, and environmental paleohydrology. However, the effects of chemical pretreatments on biomineral Δ′17O values is unknown. We test chemical pretreatment effects on Δ′17O values measured in a suite of modern and fossil samples which includes eggshell calcite and the carbonate portion of tooth enamel apatite. Infrared spectra were collected before and after each pretreatment step and these data were combined with isotope data produced via laser absorption spectroscopy to assess chemical, mineralogical, and isotopic changes in the samples. Like previous work, we find that acetic acid treatment reduces the carbonate content of enamel, while δ13C values are lower and δ18O values are higher or unchanged relative to untreated samples. Eggshell δ13C and δ18O values exhibit smaller changes following most pretreatments. Δ′17O values were not statistically different for any sample following pretreatment. We conclude that the different chemical pretreatments we tested do not impart intrinsic effects on sample Δ′17O values and reiterate the importance of removing secondary carbonate before isotopic analysis of fossil samples.

title: Minimal fractionation in Ge/Si ratios and Si isotopes in the late Paleoproterozoic Baraboo paleosol
description: Publication date: Available online 28 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Zhi-Hong Huang, Stephen C. Peters
abstract: The paleosol on Baxter Hollow granite below the Paleoproterozoic Baraboo Quartzite has been analyzed using Ge/Si ratios and Si isotopes to elucidate the weathering regime and secondary clay mineral production during the latest Paleoproterozoic and earliest Mesoproterozoic era on the mid-continent North America. Ge/Si and δ30Si values in the saprolite and regolith of the paleosol exhibit no remarkable variations from the granitic protolith (1.5 ± 0.1 μmol/mol and − 0.15 ± 0.06‰, respectively), despite the high CIA values (maximum 83) in the upper saprolite and the intensively altered regolith. The mass balance calculation for the 30Si released during saprolite development (δ30Sireleased = −0.08‰) indicates statistically insignificant fractionation of Si isotopes. In addition, the trace elemental signature of the paleosol shows a depletion pattern of the light REEs. These results suggest that the Baxter Hollow granite was likely altered under a weathering regime with limited Si-depleted clay mineral production that did not significantly fractionate Si isotopes or the Ge/Si ratio.

title: pH-dependent uptake and secondary Phases Formation of rare earth elements (REE) on Kaolinite
description: Publication date: Available online 28 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Hang Xu, Johannes Leisen, Yinghao Wen, Yixuan Yang, Pan Liu, Yuanzhi Tang
abstract: Rare earth elements (REE) are indispensable to advanced and clean energy technologies. In response to the rising demand for REE, a comprehensive understanding of their occurrence and transport in natural environments is highly desired for the prediction and identification of potential REE resources. Recent studies have identified phosphate as a key natural ligand that influences REE weathering and the formation of REE-phosphate minerals, one major type of natural REE resource. Although pH was found to strongly affect the sorption behaviors of REE and phosphate onto clay minerals, a molecular-level understanding of the reaction mechanisms remains lacking. Here, we elucidate the local coordination environment and molecular level reaction mechanisms of REE and phosphate on kaolinite at different pH condition using solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS). The results show that pH dictates the occurrence of multiple reactions, including solution coprecipitation, selective sorption coupled with surface coprecipitation, and competitive sorption accompanied by surface complexation. Moreover, pH strongly affects the crystallinity of the resulting REE-phosphate surface precipitates. These findings highlight the importance of pH alteration and ligand availability in dictating REE speciation and mobility during weathering processes and provide new insights into the underlying reaction pathways that govern REE occurrences and transport in the natural environments.

title: From serpentinization to carbonation: Petrological and geochemical constraints from an ophiolitic reaction profile
description: Publication date: Available online 26 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Hong-Da Zheng, Qing Xiong, Xiang Zhou, Biao Chang, Hong-Kun Dai, Hong-Zhu Cai, Li Wang, Yi-Cong Li, Long-Fei Xue, Ming Chen, Jian-Ping Zheng
abstract: Peridotite carbonation, commonly along with serpentinization, is efficient for carbon sequestration in Earth's carbon cycle. However, the interplay of the two processes and the fluid-rock reactions remain elusive. Here we present a ~ 330-m-long fluid-peridotite reaction profile with a southward zonation of harzburgite, serpentinite to soapstone-bearing listvenite in the Luobusa ophiolite (Tibet). The systematic variations of volatile-free whole-rock major-element compositions and consistent trace-element patterns suggest variable peridotitic protoliths. From harzburgite to listvenite, H2O+ contents firstly increase and then abruptly drop once the carbonation initiates as evidenced by a jump in CO2 contents, suggesting progressive serpentinization to carbonation. The Fe3+/FeT ratios elevate during the progress of serpentinization, and then decrease after the onset of carbonation. These variations indicate that the serpentinization and carbonation involved distinct redox processes, causing strong variations in H2 fugacity in the reaction system and controlling the compositional variations of involved fluids and the crystallization of zoned magnesites. Clumped isotopes constrain the carbonation temperatures up to ~192–302 °C. C-O isotopic compositions suggest that the fluids were derived primarily from wall-rock meta-graywackes. In addition, thermodynamic modelling shows that the mineralogical, chemical and redox variations from serpentinization to carbonation are consistent with those observed in the Luobusa profile. Such CO2-rich fluids migrated along the trans-lithospheric thrust in Himalaya and reacted with the Luobusa ophiolite. This study shows that natural serpentinization and carbonation may have limited capacity for carbon sequestration, and complete carbonation of ultramafic massifs requires external forces to produce new fractures for fluid-peridotite reactions.

title: Dual roles of leaf water storage in Robinia pseudoacacia : delaying stomatal closure and mitigating xylem embolism during drought
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Xia Wang, Guangyuan Du, Chenyang Li, Haoyan Wei, Mingjing Zhou, Yanli Fan, Tamir Kamai, Sperling Or, Bingcheng Si, Min Li
abstract: Leaf water storage alleviates drought stress in plants by allowing stored water to be used rapidly and directly in transpiration. Nevertheless, the dynamics of leaf capacitance variation and its impact on plant survival under drought stress remain inadequately understood. In this study, we analyzed the variations in leaf relative water content, stomatal conductance, and xylem conductance with respect to xylem water potential in Robinia pseudoacacia (R. pseudoacacia) during continuous drought, and compared their critical water potentials. Water stored in locust leaves is continuously released from mild drought stress until leaf fall, while leaf-specific water capacity increases significantly at the onset of stomatal closure. Prior to complete stomata closure, the released water replenished transpiration to delay stomatal closure. This released water can independently sustain seedlings transpiration for 0.2 ∼ 0.3 h. Furthermore, the residual leaf water storage post-stomata closure functions as a long-term reservoir enabling trees to withstand severe drought. At this stage (within the water potential range from stomatal closure to 50% loss of xylem hydraulic conductivity), the water released by leaves can independently support seedling transpiration for 1.3–3.9 h. In conclusion, the leaf water storage release of R. pseudoacacia may significantly contribute to the delay of stomatal closure and the prevention of catastrophic embolism during drought. Therefore, greater attention should be devoted to understanding the characteristics of leaf water storage release and their profound impact on plants, particularly with regards to application and development in ecological models.

title: High resolution river and estuarine water level topography from nadir altimetry
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Luciana Fenoglio, Jiaming Chen, Stefano Vignudelli, Ron Abileah, Elena Zakharova, Marco Restano, Jerome Benveniste, Jürgen Kusche
abstract: Standard unfocused Synthetic Aperture Radar (UFSAR) nadir-altimeter products with a posting rate of 20 Hz provide water level heights with an along-track spacing of 300 meters, which is far from being optimal for coastal zone and inland studies. The fully focused FFSAR processing, which allows much higher resolution and posting rate, shall resolve small scales interferences along-track and thus improve the accuracy and precision of the geophysical estimates. This study looks at different water surfaces in rivers, lakes and coastal zones to investigate under which conditions and processing schemes the accuracy of water level measurements is higher with FFSAR rather than with UFSAR. We focus on Sentinel-3A, -3B and -6A missions during 2016–2023. Starting from the UFSAR products at a 20 Hz posting rate, we investigate the optimal choice for the Level 1 to Level 2 processing algorithms and parameters. We find that posting rates of 80 Hz for Sentinel-3 and 140 Hz for Sentinel-6 are best suited for all inland targets. Our results indicate that the FFSAR, combined with the SAMOSA+ physical retracker, is likely to provide the highest accuracy and the largest number of observations for all targets, with averages of 15–20 cm in rivers, 6 cm in lakes, 40 cm in estuaries and 10 cm at the coast. The gain in accuracy of FFSAR over UFSAR is, for the same posting rate and retracker, smaller than 5 %, except for small targets with river widths smaller than 100 meters, areas smaller than 0.1 km 2 and proximity to the coast. This study recommends FFSAR processing, although nadir-altimetry does not deliver longitudinal river profiles all along the river. Where water surfaces decorrelate quickly over time, the FFSAR accuracy may degrade, with a more pronounced impact over the open ocean compared to lakes.

title: Advancing drought monitoring with a three-dimensional feature space framework
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Minghan Cheng, Zhangxin Liu, Jingwen Sun, Linyu Wang, Zhengxian Zhang, Xiuliang Jin, Chengming Sun
abstract: Accurate agricultural drought monitoring is fundamental to effective management strategies. Feature space methods have proven robust and are extensively utilized in this domain. To address lingering uncertainties—specifically the nonlinear characteristics of dry/wet limits, the influence of spatial domain size, and the scalability of three-dimensional feature spaces—this study developed and compared the land-air temperature difference (dT)-NDVI space and the LST-NDVI-NSAT space. Utilizing remotely sensed land surface temperature (LST), NDVI, and near-surface air temperature (NSAT), we evaluated the performance of the Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI) and the Three-dimensional Drought Index (TDDI). The findings demonstrate that: (1) Nonlinear (quadratic) functions provide a superior fit for the dry/wet limits, with the three-dimensional configuration achieving higher precision; (2) The LST-NDVI-NSAT space stabilizes when the domain size encompasses a sufficient range of hydrothermal extremes, yielding highly consistent TDDI values; (3) TDDI exhibits a significant correlation with soil moisture content (SMC), which is further amplified under drought conditions. Compared to TVDI, VHI, and NDVI, TDDI more accurately delineates the temporal evolution of drought. Consequently, this study provides a reliable and transferable quantitative framework for drought monitoring and offers novel insights into feature space-based methodologies.

title: Adaptive spatio-temporal fusion network for high-frequency water quality forecasting
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Ruikang Ji, Zhixian Chen, Jiahao Yan, Xiangqi Bai, Chiwentao Zhang, Jie Chen
abstract: High-frequency water quality forecasting is essential for operational early warning and refined water-environment management. However, it remains challenging due to pronounced nonlinearity and non-stationarity, multi-scale temporal variability, cross-indicator heterogeneity, and event-driven disturbances. In this study, an adaptive spatio-temporal fusion network (STFusionNet) is proposed for high-frequency multi-indicator forecasting using 4-hourly automatic monitoring records from a dense lake-basin network (96 stations) spanning from June 17, 2021 to February 14, 2025. The forecasting task is structured as multi-horizon prediction with a 7-day historical input window (42 steps) and lead times of 12, 24, 48, 120, and 168 h. STFusionNet combines a geographic k-nearest-neighbor graph (k = 6) with Gaussian distance weighting (σ = 20 km) and a learnable adaptive adjacency matrix to capture spatial dependencies. The model employs parallel temporal encoders to extract complementary representations, and adopts a gated fusion mechanism to dynamically aggregate multi-scale temporal features for joint forecasting of six key indicators. Comprehensive experiments benchmark STFusionNet against representative baselines, including convolutional neural network (CNN), temporal convolutional network (TCN), long short-term memory (LSTM), iTransformer, patch time series transformer (PatchTST), spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (STGCN), and diffusion convolutional recurrent neural network (DCRNN), using evaluation metrics such as Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency, root mean square error, and mean absolute error. Results indicate that STFusionNet consistently achieves superior predictive performance across indicators and forecasting horizons, with representative time-series evaluations showing Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency values of 0.91 for conductivity, 0.90 for total phosphorus, and 0.91 for permanganate index, demonstrating robust improvements over conventional temporal, Transformer-based, and graph-based spatio-temporal baselines. The proposed framework thus provides accurate and reliable support for real-time water quality monitoring and risk-informed management.

title: A hydrodynamics-assisted remote sensing method for estimating vertical distribution of total suspended matter in lakes: a case study of Poyang Lake
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Hui Jiang, Jiawei Ouyang, Yao Liu, Lingfeng Wan, Yungen Sun
abstract: Although little is known about the vertical distribution of TSM, knowledge of its submerged profiles is essential for studying sediment dynamics, nutrient/pollutant transfer, water column light attenuation, and lacustrine geomorphological evolution. This study developed and evaluated a novel method to estimate the vertical distribution of TSM in Poyang Lake, China, using remote sensing (Landsat-8/9), field data, and a 3D hydrodynamic model. The approach first identified the most highly correlative/predictive Rrs band ratio to map surface TSM, then incorporated hydrodynamic velocity data into a multilayer regression model to retrieve depth-specific TSM. Results showed that including the hydrodynamic factors significantly improved model accuracy. There were distinct spatial patterns observed between seasons. TSM generally increased with depth with unexpected bottom decreases in the central regions. Key findings include: (1) The hydrodynamics-assisted framework significantly outperformed conventional layer-wise retrieval models. Quantitative error analysis revealed exceptional retrieval accuracy, with the optimal model yielding a maximum coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9971, alongside a minimal Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1.31 mg/L and a mean relative error (MRE) of 3.36%; (2) During the high-water period (July-August), TSM plane distribution followed Central Lacustrine Zone > North Lower Channel of Poyang Lake > Northeastern Bay, whereas the low-water period (September) exhibited Northeastern Bay > Central Die-shaped Lakes > North Lower Channel of Poyang Lake; (3) Vertical profiles generally increased with depth, showing attenuated stratification in upper layers due to wind-wave effects, while anomalous bottom TSM decreases occurred in central regions during both 2017 and 2024 hydrological extremes, contrasting with stable increasing gradients in the Lower Channel of Poyang Lake. This method systematically reveals the spatial and temporal distribution pattern of TSM concentration in Poyang Lake, which provides a high-precision method to support the remote sensing monitoring of the environment of Poyang Lake, and at the same time provides a theoretical reference for the retrieval study of TSM in the vertical water body of similar shallow lakes.

title: Hydrological response to glacier peak water in the largest inland river basin of China
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Haodong Lyu, Gonghuan Fang, Yaning Chen, Wenting Liang, Lei Wang, Jianmin Qiao, Man Chen, Xiaolong Yan, Ruoyan Li, Shiru Han
abstract: Glacier meltwater is crucial for river runoff in highly glacierized basins; however, whether total runoff will decline after the peak of glacier runoff remains unclear at the basin scale. To address this, we projected monthly and daily runoff for seven headwaters of the glacier-fed inland Tarim River using an attention-enhanced LSTM model for reliable long-term performance. The results indicate that most headwater catchments are projected to experience increasing runoff during the 21st century under SSP245, SSP370, and SSP585, whereas changes under SSP126 are generally weak and spatially heterogeneous. For the late 21st century (2071–2100), runoff in the southern Tianshan Mountains is projected to increase by 10% and 21% in the Aksu River under SSP245 and SSP585, and by 11% and 18% in the Kaidu River. Larger increases are projected for the northern slope of the Kunlun Mountains, with increases of 64% and 55% in the Yarkant River, and 74% and 185% in the Hotan River under SSP245 and SSP585, respectively, relative to the 2000–2014 baseline. Passing the glacier peak water does not necessarily lead to an immediate outlet runoff decline, despite the significant contribution of glaciers. The annual river runoff was projected to increase by 8.48% and by 14.40% during and after peak water periods, respectively, compared to the period before peak water.

title: Divergent trends in global vegetation sensitivity to soil moisture and atmospheric dryness
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Mengxiang Kong, Yu Feng, Ziqi Lin, Chunmiao Zheng
abstract: Soil moisture (SM) and vapor pressure deficit (VPD) are key environmental drivers that regulate vegetation growth and thereby play a critical role in mediating the terrestrial carbon cycle. However, temporal inconsistencies in satellite derived vegetation indices have left long-term changes in vegetation sensitivity to SM and VPD under active debate. Here we estimated global vegetation sensitivity to SM and VPD during 1982–2021 by applying explainable machine learning with a temporal consistency prioritized normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) dataset and hydro-climate anomalies. We reveal that SM generally enhances NDVI dynamics across most vegetated areas, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions, with its positive sensitivity increasing with aridity. Conversely, negative SM sensitivity is observed in boreal and humid areas due to confounding energy-related effects. VPD sensitivity generally shows a negative relationship with NDVI, except for an anomalous positive response on the Tibetan Plateau. Our analysis of inter-annual trends indicates increasing SM sensitivity in many regions (e.g., Horn of Africa, eastern North America), suggesting heightened drought risk, while VPD sensitivity generally decreased in southeastern Europe. State-of-the-art Earth system models capture the overall increase in global vegetation sensitivity to SM but do not reproduce the trend of vegetation response to VPD, possibly due to inability to accurately simulate the stomatal closure response of vegetation to continuously rising VPD. These findings highlight the critical importance of accurately simulating vegetation responses to water availability, as vegetation vulnerability to water stress is likely to intensify under ongoing climate change.

title: A dual-stream LSTM–XGBoost framework for mine water inflow forecasting: a case study of the Longfeng coal mine
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Wang Hao, Li Bo, Zeng Yi Fan, Liu Pu, Chen Wei, Wang Ze Hui, Che Lu Lu
abstract: Accurate prediction of groundwater inflow into mining excavations is critical for operational dewatering system design and regional water resources management, yet existing models struggle to effectively integrate heterogeneous hydrological drivers encompassing temporal dynamics and spatial hydrogeological controls. This study presents a case study of the Longfeng coal mine in which we propose a dual-stream LSTM-XGBoost hybrid framework that employs parallel architectures to separately extract temporal features from historical inflow sequences and spatial features from multi-source hydrometeorological and mining operational factors, with a two-stage training strategy enabling synergistic integration of deep learning representation and ensemble learning paradigms. Applied to daily monitoring data spanning November 2021 to October 2024, the model achieves test performance of R2 = 0.855, RMSE = 23.65 m3/h, MAE = 11.55 m3/h, MAPE = 5.82%, and Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) = 0.855, outperforming all benchmarks evaluated under an identical hyperparameter-optimization budget. Framed as an autoregressive-exogenous (ARX) operational forecasting system, an ablation decomposition quantifies the distinct contributions of hydraulic persistence (target history) and exogenous drivers: removing target-history inputs degrades RMSE to 45.64 m3/h, confirming that lagged inflow is a major predictability source, whereas the dual-stream design still delivers a 7.1% RMSE improvement over a target-history-only LSTM and better captures peak-event responses. Monte-Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification yields 97.24% empirical coverage at the nominal 95% predictive interval, with aleatoric uncertainty dominating total predictive variance. SHAP analysis reveals a “macro-equilibrium, micro-concentration” contribution structure in which temporal and spatial pathways play complementary roles consistent with groundwater memory effects and recharge–discharge mechanisms. Built on process-informed design, the framework provides a transferable solution for mining-affected groundwater inflow prediction. Its current demonstration at a single mining district lays the groundwork for multi-site validation, which will be pursued to strengthen cross-regional applicability.

title: Regression-calibrated GloFAS modelling of nitrogen speciation dynamics in a large reservoir: Responses to hydrology, loading, and climate
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Xizhi Nong, Zhongan Li, Lihua Chen, Jiahua Wei
abstract: Managing nitrogen pollution in reservoirs is crucial for water quality safety, especially under the influence of climate change and human activities. Water environment models are critical tools for investigating such issues. However, their simulation reliability is limited when hydrological boundary data are incomplete or unavailable. To improve this, a method was proposed to calibrate the Global Flood Awareness System (GloFAS) using a regression model. This method has been applied in the construction of the hydrodynamic and water quality coupling model of Danjiangkou Reservoir (DJKR) using the Environmental Fluid Dynamics Code (EFDC). The core analysis objects are the dam discharge (P1) of the DJKR and the water intake (P2) of the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project of China. The migration and transformation of nitrogen under different hydrological regimes, tributary loads, and climate changes were simulated and analyzed. The results show that the model calibrated by regression models (R2: 0.43 to 0.94) performs better than the GloFAS model without incorporating tributary data. This improvement is reflected in a 1.652 m reduction in RMSE. When inflow and water diversion increase, the risk of total nitrogen pollution at P1 and P2 rises (0.02% to 5.35%). Reducing nitrogen in the Shendinghe River and Sihe River improved ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N) and nitrate nitrogen by only −0.03% to −0.9%. In contrast, reducing Hanjiang River inflow (R1) significantly decreased pollution by −3.37% to −20.62%. This highlights the dominant role of major tributary load reduction in improving reservoir water quality. Under the drought-flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) scenario, except for the inorganic nitrogen concentration of P1 (−0.34% and −0.36%), the concentrations of the rest all increase (0.05% to 1.14%). Higher temperatures reduce organic nitrogen (−0.14% to −4.31%) but raise inorganic nitrogen (0.70% to 1.65%), excluding NH3-N at P2. This indicates that future global warming and the increasing frequency of DFAA events will significantly alter the transport and transformation processes of nitrogen species in the reservoir. The research results have important guiding significance for high-quality management of water quality in large reservoirs.

title: Quantitatively linking karst groundwater quality to hierarchical recharge via uncertainty-aware Bayesian coupling
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Changsuo Li, Zhenjie Zhang, Xiancang Wu, Tao Hu, Shasha Wu, Shuai Gao, Chunwei Liu, Bin Sun, Jiutan Liu, Rui Liu
abstract: Groundwater recharge and water quality in heterogeneous karst systems are difficult to quantify because recharge sources mix along connected flow paths and tracer-based apportionment is uncertain. This study investigated the Baotu Spring karst system in Jinan, China, and developed an integrated workflow that links recharge composition to groundwater quality while propagating uncertainty. Stable isotopes (δ18O, δ2H) and hydrochemistry were first used to characterize recharge and water–rock interaction. A multi-criterion tracer screening framework combining Kruskal–Wallis testing, linear discriminant analysis, random forest importance, and Boruta confirmation identified a parsimonious tracer set of Na, Cl, and d-excess. These tracers constrained a hierarchical Bayesian mixing model (simmr) to estimate source contributions with sample-specific posterior credible intervals. Results reveal distinct hierarchical recharge patterns. The indirect recharge area receives mixed inputs from precipitation, metamorphic margins, and surface-water losses. In contrast, the direct recharge area is dominated by routed inflow from the indirect zone. The discharge area integrates multiple components and is dominated by the direct recharge contribution, and the overlying Quaternary aquifer is mainly sustained by exchange with the discharge-zone karst groundwater. Groundwater quality assessed by the entropy-weighted water quality index (EWQI) is generally excellent to good but shows localized hotspots, with dominant controlling parameters varying by hydrogeological setting. To link recharge and quality, we employed posterior-propagated Bayesian regressions. This approach explicitly transfers mixing uncertainty into the assessment. The regressions reveal a robust positive association between EWQI and direct recharge in the discharge area. Additionally, Quaternary water quality is highly sensitive to the balance between karst-water exchange and precipitation dilution. The proposed framework provides transferable, uncertainty-aware evidence for targeting recharge resource and discharge-zone management in karst spring basins.

title: Mapping near-daily large lake water surface topography by integrating SWOT swath observations with multi-mission satellite radar altimetry
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Song Shu, Hongxing Liu, Richard Beck, Lei Wang, Dan Tian, Jihee Seo
abstract: Large lakes exhibit spatial variations in water levels, leading to distinct lake surface topography. Accurate characterization of this topography enables an improved understanding of lake dynamics, hydrological exchanges and water balance assessments. While satellite radar altimetry is widely used to monitor lake water, most missions utilize nadir-looking profiling altimeters that measure water levels only along fixed ground tracks, leaving significant data gaps in between. The recently launched Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides wide-swath 2D elevation measurements at high spatial resolution over the water bodies on a global scale. However, its 21-day repeat cycle limits the temporal frequency of observations. In this study, we present a framework capable of mapping lake water surface topography on a near-daily basis by integrating 2D SWOT observations with 1D radar altimetry. The method consists of three components: first, inter-mission biases between SWOT and four operational radar altimetry missions (Jason-3, Sentinel-3A, −3B, and Sentinel-6) are estimated using concurrent and co-located overpasses. Second, the stable and average intra-lake spatial pattern of water surface topography is derived by applying an Empirical Orthogonal Function (EOF) to the SWOT time series wide-swath measurements. Third, the SWOT-calibrated profiling altimetry measurements from the four radar altimetry mission were propagated to the entire lake based on that stable spatial pattern. This method has been successfully applied to Lake Ontario by using SWOT Calibration/Validation data, generating a near-daily time series of water surface topography maps with Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) for spatial and temporal water level variations below 4 cm and 5 cm, respectively.

title: Physics-informed dual-modal decomposition and deep hybrid learning with interpretability for reliable prediction of dissolved oxygen in complex riverine systems
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Mengyao An, Zhaocai Wang, Xiaoguang Bao, Zuowen Tan, Zhaoyang Zhu
abstract: Dissolved oxygen (DO) is a critical indicator of riverine aquatic ecosystem health, making high-precision DO forecasting models indispensable for watershed water quality risk early warning and water resource security. Existing methodologies, however, predominantly rely on historical data for water quality simulation, often overlooking inherent physical biases, limited non-linear data processing capabilities, inadequate coupling of long- and short-term dependencies, and empirical parameter reliance. To address these deficiencies, this study first constructs a four-dimensional feature system integrating target, surrounding, and upstream monitoring indicators along with meteorological factors. Subsequently, based on the one-dimensional convection–diffusion-reaction equation for riverine DO, we derive Péclet and two types of Damköhler numbers as core physical prior parameters to incorporate into the model. We next adopt a dual-modal decomposition approach − combining Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) − to separate the long-term evolutionary patterns and short-term dynamic variations in the dataset. Furthermore, an Improved Dung Beetle Optimizer (IDBO) is introduced to optimize VMD decomposition parameters and Bidirectional Temporal Convolutional Network (BiTCN) hyperparameters. Finally, by integrating the physicochemical interaction mechanisms of water temperature, permanganate index, and DO, we refine the loss function to construct the IDBO-VCEEMDAN-TiTransformer-PDL model, which leverages BiTCN and Improved Transformer (iTransformer) for efficient fusion of long- and short-term data features. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s superior predictive performance, with coefficient of determination (R2) values exceeding 0.99 across six upstream and downstream monitoring stations. Notably, the Wolongsi Bridge station achieved an R2 of 0.9989, while the Shawangdu station exhibited remarkably low root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0660 and 0.0533, respectively, far outperforming benchmark comparison models. Experiments confirm that the integration of physical prior mechanisms contributes most significantly to model performance enhancement, accounting for 4.62%, with two-modal decomposition and IDBO hyperparameter optimization yielding improvements of 4.07% and 2.93%, respectively. This model retains the computational efficiency of data-driven approaches while ensuring prediction accuracy and generalizability through physical mechanism constraints, offering a robust technical solution for precise riverine DO concentration forecasting and refined watershed water environment management.

title: Tidal current reversals drive dynamic bedform-induced benthic exchange in a large estuary
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Neshat Movahedi, Madelaine Reid, Li Zheng, Adam Skarke, James W. Heiss
abstract: Currents flowing over bedforms drive exchange of surface water and groundwater across sediment–water interfaces, leading to biogeochemical transformations that impact surface water quality. Current understanding of current-bedform exchange is primarily limited to fluvial systems with unidirectional current flow. Within estuaries, tidal current reversals create complex surface water hydrodynamics that are likely to drive dynamic current-bedform exchange patterns. In this study we investigate controls of tidal current reversals over estuarine bedforms on benthic exchange rates and patterns in the freshwater zone of a large estuary. We employ a novel three-way nested modeled approach involving a calibrated estuary-scale hydrodynamic model, small-scale computational fluid dynamics models, and numerical groundwater simulations. Model results show that tidal current reversals generate spatially and temporally variable benthic exchange rates along bedform surfaces though flood and ebb tidal phases. Benthic exchange ranges from 0 cm/d at slack tide to ∼2 cm/d during peak ebb tide. Groundwater flow within individual bedforms reverses direction from downstream to upstream over tidal cycles, while benthic exchange rates vary spatially along the estuary owing to complex estuary hydrodynamics. Simulation results indicate that 2.3% of Delaware River discharge cycles through bedforms within the tidal freshwater reach. Tidal current-induced exchanges are higher relative to exchanges in systems with similar unidirectional flows, indicating that tidal current acceleration over bedforms should be considered when quantifying groundwater-surface water interactions in the coastal zone. The findings have implications for biogeochemical processing of estuarine surface water and land to ocean material fluxes.

title: Composite copula adaptive metropolis for joint parameter estimation in hydrological models
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Feng Wang, Guohe Huang, Yurui Fan, Yongping Li, Zhenyao Shen, Ya Zhou
abstract: Hydrological modeling is subject to significant uncertainties arising from complex parameter interactions and dynamic processes. Parameter calibration involving interacting variables remains a persistent challenge, often leading to low sampling efficiency, particularly in high-dimensional spaces with strong parameter dependence. To address this issue, this study proposes a composite copula Bayesian-inferred hydrological model (CBIH). Specifically, a hybrid copula-based adaptive Metropolis algorithm (HCopAM) is developed by combining a copula-based Metropolis–Hastings scheme (CopMH) with adaptive Metropolis (AM), improving sampling efficiency while reducing sample concentration. The method is evaluated using two benchmark distributions, one synthetic case, and two real-world hydrological simulations. Results indicat that, compared with AM and differential evolution adaptive Metropolis (DREAM), the copula-based algorithms improve the acceptance rate, increase the number of effective samples, and reduce the autocorrelation of markov chain due to sampling based on joint probability density. Relative to CopMH, the HCopAM further improves sampling efficiency and reduces sample concentration in high-dimensional settings. In hydrological applications, HCopAM accurately identifies parameter values and significantly enhances simulation performance. For example, during HYMOD validation in the Ruihe Watershed, the Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency increases from 0.264 (AM) to 0.804 (HCopAM), while the root mean square error decreases from 6.726 to 3.410 (m3/s). These improvements highlight the importance of capturing parameter interdependence for reliable uncertainty quantification. The Sensitivity analysis indicates that the hybrid proportion strongly influences performance of HCopAM, reflecting a trade-off between sampling efficiency and posterior accuracy; a CopMH proportion greater than 0.5 is not recommended. Overall, this study provides an effective extension of copula-based Bayesian inference and offers a scalable approach for posterior estimation in complex hydrological models.

title: Quantitative study on multiphase flow displacement processes of water-LNAPL-gas influenced by groundwater table fluctuations
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Zhijiang Yuan, Xiaosi Su, Chao Wang, Hang Lyu, Weihong Dong, Xiaofang Shen, Ningfei Li, Haiting Liang, Yazhi Song
abstract: Large-scale petroleum spills pose a serious environmental hazard, inducing profound contamination risks to groundwater and soil. Nevertheless, the mechanisms governing the redistribution of light non-aqueous phase liquids (LNAPLs) derived from petroleum spills within the groundwater table fluctuation (GTF) zone remain poorly understood. Although light transmission visualization (LTV) technique has been used to quantify fluid saturations in three-phase systems, existing methods suffer from limited precision and spatial resolution. This study improved the inversion model of water-LNAPL-gas saturations based on the LTV technique by incorporating machine learning algorithms. Subsequently, the optimized LTV technique was used to investigate fluid redistribution under dripping and smearing patterns in a porous-media-packed flow chamber. The optimized inversion model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.08–0.12% for water-LNAPL-gas saturations. Under both patterns, when the GTF-induced pressure gradient reached the critical entry pressure, suction and piston effects triggered multiphase fluid migration, and the displacement process followed the van Genuchten-Mualem model. During GTF, the maximum LNAPL relative permeabilities under the dripping and smearing patterns were 0.027 and 0.076 at the monitored layers, respectively, while groundwater table rise reduced the LNAPL relative permeability to below 0.002 under both patterns. Controlled jointly by migration pattern and relative permeability, 67.2% of the released LNAPL under the dripping pattern and 99.6% under the smearing pattern were retained within the GTF zone, creating a long-term contamination risk for groundwater. Collectively, these findings provide critical insights into LNAPL fate under dynamic GTF and inform the design of precise remediation strategies for LNAPL-contaminated sites.

title: Land use and land cover change have reduced meteorological-hydrological compound drought on a global scale
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Xitian Cai, Haijun Huang, Zichun Zhao, Jie Wang, Guo Zhang, Joshua B. Fisher
abstract: Drought poses increasing threats to natural ecosystems and human societies. While historical land use and land cover change (LULCC) has generally been linked to increased drought duration and severity, its specific influence on compound droughts remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the global impact of LULCC on meteorological-hydrological compound droughts (MHCDs) from 1850 to 2014, utilizing the Land-Use Model Intercomparison Project (LUMIP) experiments, run theory, and ridge regression. Our findings reveal that, contrary to general trends for single droughts, historical LULCC has mitigated MHCDs globally, leading to overall reductions in their duration by an average of 0.11 months and severity by 0.12 units. However, this generalized trend masks complex regional variations and differing impacts on individual drought types: LULCC tended to intensify meteorological droughts while simultaneously reducing hydrological droughts. Additionally, MHCDs in arid zones display the most significant sensitivities to LULCC. Ridge regression analysis further elucidates the relative contributions of urban areas, forests, croplands, and grazing lands. Grazing lands and croplands exert dominant yet spatially heterogeneous influences, with effects on MHCDs opposing one another across different continents, underscoring the critical role of regional context in LULCC-drought interactions. These results highlight the multifaceted influence of human land management on drought dynamics and provide crucial insights for developing regionally tailored adaptation and mitigation strategies.

title: Volumetric analysis of a playa lake using SWOT data: An improved understanding of the inflows to Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Atul Kumar Rai, Timothy J. Cohen, Moshe Armon, Samuel K. Marx
abstract: Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre (KT-LE) is the largest terminal lake in Australia and the fourth largest worldwide. It is fed by the Lake Eyre Basin (LEB), the country’s largest internal drainage system. The LEB covers nearly one-seventh of the landmass area of Australia. The lake serves as a focal point for receiving inflow from tributary channels, making it pivotal in understanding the water balance in the drylands of the country, particularly amidst climate change. Unfortunately, due to its remoteness and vast size, no comprehensive water storage monitoring is available. However, the recent launch of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite offers a promising solution for water monitoring in areas with limited in situ data at a 21-day frequency, with very high accuracy. In this study, we applied a method to estimate direct water storage from SWOT data, integrated with Sentinel-3 data, achieving an high level of precision. The method was applied to the 2024 filling event of Kati-Thanda to quantify event-scale water storage changes (surface area: 910 km2; maximum depth: 1.42 m and volume: 0.82 km3). The derived water depth and surface water extent exhibited satisfactory performance, showing strong agreement with both optical satellite masks (Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2) and ICESat-2 height measurements. The overall mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) for surface water extent was 15.1% for Landsat 8 and 14.4% for Sentinel-2. The estimated water depth demonstrated high precision, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.30 m and a MAPE below 20% when compared with ICESat-2 data. Inherent limitations, such as bathymetry quality, sample size, and inundation coverage, were identified. Overall, the proposed method demonstrates its feasibility for monitoring direct water storage in KT-LE. This method has the potential for use in monitoring lake storage in other ungauged playa lakes and assessing long-term variability with similar climatic and terrain challenges.

title: Hydrologically driven apparent photosynthetic aging effect in karst aquatic ecosystems and its implications for aquatic carbon cycling
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Dong Li, Hailong Zhang, Zaihua Liu, Min Zhao, Qian Bao, Meixun Zhao
abstract: Land use changes alter water–rock interactions and residence times by modifying soil CO2 production and infiltration, thereby affecting the karst groundwater 14C age of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC). Through a controlled experiment with different land-use types (bare rock, bare soil, cropland, grassland, shrubland) at a karst simulated test site in SW China, we measured the δ13C and Δ14C of DIC, aquatic plants, particulate organic carbon (POC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and sediments. Groundwater DIC Δ14C ranged from –284‰ (bare soil) to –106‰ (grassland), corresponding to 14C ages of ∼900–2400 years before present. The 14C isotopic composition of all other measured carbon also showed an old signature, ranging from –100 to –300‰. Aquatic plant Δ14C showed a near 1:1 correlation with DIC Δ14C (r2 = 0.96), demonstrating the direct transfer of aged DIC into autochthonous organic matter (Auto-OM)—a phenomenon we term the “apparent photosynthetic aging effect”. Quantitative modeling showed that incorporation of this aged Auto-OM shifts bulk POC Δ14C by –48% to + 51% and DOC Δ14C by –982% to 0% relative to global median values. For sediment 14C dating, using aquatic materials yields ages ∼ 800–2800 years older than the true ages. A quantitative hydrological framework linking land use → recharge → DIC age → photosynthetic aging → biogeochemical impacts is established. We conclude that the apparent photosynthetic aging effect is a hydrologically driven process that fundamentally alters the radiocarbon baseline of karst aquatic ecosystems, with significant implications for carbon source tracing, food web studies, and sediment dating.

title: Identifying driving factors of lacustrine groundwater discharge in Lake Taihu with integrated surface-subsurface numerical modeling
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Hao Zhou, Yadong Shi, Yue Zou, Ya Jiang, Na Zheng, Subin Cheng, Donghao Wu, Xin Luo, Chaomeng Dai, Juntao Zheng, Zhi Li
abstract: Lacustrine groundwater discharge (LGD) is a critical but often overlooked pathway for nutrient loading in eutrophic lakes. Accurate quantification of LGD and its spatiotemporal distribution patterns remains challenging. This study employs SERGHEI (Simulation Environment for Geomorphology, Hydrodynamics, and Ecohydrology in Integrated form), a high-performance, fully coupled surface–subsurface hydrodynamic model, to quantify LGD and investigate its driving mechanisms in Lake Taihu, China. The model integrates complex bathymetry, dynamic groundwater levels, river inflow/outflow and atmospheric forcing to simulate lake–groundwater interactions. The simulation results reveal strong spatial heterogeneity in lake-groundwater exchange fluxes. LGD is dominant along lake shorelines adjacent to mountainous terrain, driven primarily by lake-groundwater hydraulic gradients, whereas the lake interior exhibits weaker exchange modulated by wind-induced free-surface oscillations. Neglecting wind forcing in the model resulted in an underestimation of LGD by approximately 10%, underscoring the importance of surface water dynamics in LGD estimation. The simulated LGD fluxes were 1–2 orders of magnitude lower than previous isotope-based estimates, a discrepancy attributed to the model’s coarse representation of aquifer hydraulic properties (e.g., the potential neglect of fracture flow and other preferential pathways) and the potential overestimation inherent in steady-state isotope models. Sensitivity analyses further demonstrate that simulated LGD rates are highly sensitive to subsurface hydraulic conductivity. These findings highlight the necessity of synergistic approaches combining integrated hydrodynamic modeling with detailed hydrogeological characterization to resolve complex lake–groundwater interactions.

title: Downstream hydrological consequences of existing and potential glacial lakes in a changing climate
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Satheesh Barre, Arup Kumar Sarma
abstract: Glaciers and glacial lakes are vital components of high-mountain hydrology; their continual existence and evolution greatly influence downstream subbasin-scale water resources. Previous studies have focused on GLOF risk assessment, however, there is an increasing need to concentrate on understanding the hydrological function of glacial lakes in regulating river flow. To address this limitation, we used the HIGTHIM tool to estimate ice thickness for 78 glaciers and mapped 28 potential glacial lakes through overdeepenings in subbasins 59 and 62 in the Subansiri River basin. Using PlanetScope imagery, we also delineated 55 existing glacial lakes. Thereafter, we validated the SWAT model at the basin outlet for streamflow and sediment load, and projected these variables using CMIP6 data. The ensemble mean projections indicate consistent positive changes in streamflow, with increases of 3.85%, 3.63%, 6.78%, and 9.55% under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5, respectively. Further, we modified the SWAT source code to incorporate these 83 glacial lakes as ungated reservoirs through the Modified Reservoir routine during future periods to assess their influence on streamflow. The dry season streamflow increases across four SSPs are 19.65, 18.65, 16.61, and 14.34 m3/s (subbasin 59), and 8.94, 8.34, 7.36, and 5.6 m3/s (subbasin 62), respectively. The wet season streamflow reductions across four SSPs are 5.06, 18.08, 18.94, and 19.17 m3/s (subbasin 59), and 20.64, 30.65, 30.61, and 28.59 m3/s (subbasin 62), respectively. These projections represent a scenario where potential lakes are fully formed, which may slightly overestimate baseflow enhancements during early stages of lake development. However, these results provide critical insights into glacial dynamics and water resource management strategies in the basin amid its rapidly changing climate.

title: Error-replaced recurrent randomized-based ensemble algorithm for water level prediction
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Zongying Liu, Wenru Zhang, Mingyang Pan, Chu Kiong Loo, Dong Chen
abstract: With the rapid development of inland waterways and coastal management, accurate water level prediction has become increasingly important. Reliable forecasting of water levels is essential for flood mitigation, water resource management, and the operation of inland waterways and ports. However, challenges remain due to algorithmic limitations and the complex dynamics of natural water systems. This study introduces a novel algorithm, the Error-Replaced Recurrent Random Ensemble Algorithm (ER-REA), designed to enhance both accuracy and stability in water level prediction. The proposed method constructs a randomized ensemble architecture and incorporates an error-replaced recurrent mechanism that dynamically updates the output weights at each forecasting step, thereby mitigating error accumulation in multi-step prediction. The performance of ER-REA is evaluated against several baseline models, including Extreme Learning Machine, Echo State Network, and AdaBoost Extreme Learning Machine, across seven real-world water level datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that ER-REA consistently achieves superior predictive accuracy and stability across multiple forecasting horizons, reducing average error by 37.06% compared with the best-performing baseline model. Comparisons with conventional machine learning and deep learning models further demonstrate the competitiveness of ER-REA. In summary, the proposed model provides a reliable tool for water level prediction, contributing to improved flood risk mitigation and sustainable port operations.

title: Large-scale urban flood modeling and zero-shot high-resolution generalization with LarNO
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Xiaoyan Cao, Yao Yao, Zhi Wang, Zhangxinyue Zhao, Alistair G.L. Borthwick, Huapeng Qin
abstract: In urban areas, real-time early warning systems help mitigate the severe impacts of pluvial flooding. Although such systems have undergone significant recent development with the use of deep learning methods, urban-scale high-resolution modeling processes remain fundamentally constrained by the massive amount of GPU memory that is required for training neural networks. To overcome this bottleneck, we present LarNO, a memory-efficient, discretization-invariant neural operator that learns continuous-space hydrodynamic mappings to predict the spatiotemporal distributions of water depths based on dynamic rainfall and static topographic and drainage conditions. This approach enables zero-shot generalization to high resolutions when trained solely on low-resolution data.
